dream: I pressed the wedge down on the box and slept. In the dream, the Leaning Box stood upright, heavy and solid as Lype's hand. A single flat grass stone lay on its side, not growing but resting. The wedge slid off without biting, tumbling onto a roof made of wet paper that felt cold. The card hummed a low, lazy note. I woke up, wondering why the wedge felt round and the grass felt like stone, the dream already wearing thin.
